systems.name: Body & structure
systems.description: The body ties everything together: an enclosed passenger cell, crumple zones at both ends and a smooth exterior that guides air around the vehicle.
systems.principle: The structure carries loads around the cabin. At over 5.1 m the VF 9 is an E-segment SUV, with a hood over the front compartment and a tailgate opening onto the luggage space behind the third row.

systems.name: Glass & panoramic roof
systems.description: Windshield, side glass and the panoramic roof panel open the cabin to the outside and make all three rows feel spacious.
systems.principle: The windshield and side glazing provide visibility around the car. On the top trim a panoramic roof spans most of the ceiling. The dark tint in this model is a rendering material.

systems.name: Doors & tailgate
systems.description: Four conventionally hinged doors open onto three rows of seats; the tailgate lifts high for luggage. The door handles sit flush with the body while driving.
systems.principle: Each door is an assembly of outer panel, glass, latch, seals and interior trim. The tailgate is powered and can be operated from the key or the centre screen.

systems.name: Passenger cabin
systems.description: The cabin sits above the battery pack: three rows for six or seven people, a 15.6-inch centre display and the controls the driver uses every day.
systems.principle: The flat floor of the EV platform allows several seating layouts: seven seats with a three-seat middle row, or six with two captain's chairs. The source model has no detailed interior, so this section is reference only.

systems.name: High-voltage battery
systems.description: A liquid-cooled lithium-ion pack stores the energy for the whole vehicle. Mounted under the cabin floor, it feeds the two electric motors.
systems.principle: Under acceleration, energy flows from the pack to the motors. During regenerative braking the motors act as generators and return the car's kinetic energy to the pack.

systems.name: Electric motors
systems.description: Two electric motors turn stored energy into wheel torque. One sits on the front axle and one on the rear, giving permanent all-wheel drive.
systems.principle: An inverter controls each motor and a single-speed reduction gear transfers rotation to the wheels. The motors also slow the car through regenerative braking.

systems.name: Air suspension
systems.description: Air springs carry the body and electronically controlled dampers manage its movement. The system can change ride height and how the car responds to the road.
systems.principle: Double-wishbone front and multi-link rear suspension guide each wheel. Air pressure sets the height while damping balances comfort and control. Air suspension is fitted on the top trim.

systems.name: Wheels & brakes
systems.description: The tyres are the only contact between car and road. Behind each wheel a ventilated disc and caliper provide friction braking.
systems.principle: Regenerative braking recovers energy through the motors; friction brakes add stopping force when needed, with ABS controlling wheel slip.

pieces.interior.block: The source model has no interior; the author placed a dark block inside the cabin to hide the void when looking through the glass. The real VF 9 cabin has three rows of seats and a 15.6-inch centre display.
pieces.door.handle: Door handle. On the VF 9 the handles sit flush with the body and pop out when the car unlocks.
pieces.lens.front: The glass cover over the front LED light bar, which runs across the nose in VinFast's V-shaped design language.

notes: VF 9 figures come from VinFast's official specification page; seating, air suspension and the glass roof vary by trim.
